studies.title: Osteoprotective Effects of Melatonin on Bone Loss Associated with Dopaminergic Neuron Degeneration in a Rat Model of Parkinson Disease.
studies.abstract: Public health problems regarding the potential association between Parkinson's disease (PD) and the increased prevalence of osteoporosis have been raised. However, the exact relationship, as well as potential treatment strategies, remains unclear and requires further investigation. Melatonin (MLT) is known for its beneficial effects on bone metabolism and its strong neuroprotective properties. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the potential role of MLT in the prevention and treatment of bone loss associated with PD using an hemiparkinsonian rat model induced by the destruction of dopaminergic neurons following intracerebral injection of 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA). Forty male Wistar rats were divided into 5 groups: Control (CTR), 6-OHDA, MLT, 6-OHDA + MLT 1, and 6-OHDA + MLT 15. MLT (20 mg/kg/day) was administered intraperitoneally from Day 1 or Day 15, depending on the group. The effects on locomotor performance, oxidative status, bone structure, collagen accumulation, mineralization and the expression of bone marker proteins and genes were examined. Our results showed that the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons caused by 6-OHDA significantly impaired locomotor performance and induced marked alterations in bone parameters. Early MLT treatment (Day 1) mitigated these bone alterations by preserving structural integrity, enhancing collagen accumulation, and modulating bone marker expression. Importantly, beneficial effects on bone were also observed when MLT was administered later (Day 15), despite the absence of significant improvement in motor deficits. These findings suggest that dopaminergic neuron degeneration can negatively influence bone health and that MLT may exert a direct osteoprotective effect, supporting its possible therapeutic utility in managing bone fragility associated with PD.

studies.title: Melatonin combined with static magnetic field acquire better protective effects on bone mass and bone strength in osteoporosis induced by ovariectomy in rats.
studies.abstract:
Objective

This research aimed to examine the possible impacts of Melatonin (Mel) combined with static magnetic field (SMF) on bone mass and strength in rats with osteoporosis induced by bilateral ovary removal.

Methods

Following bilateral ovariectomy, the female ovariectomized (OVX) rats were systematically allocated into four distinct experimental groups: (1) OVX (control group), (2) OVX+melatonin (OVX+Mel), (3) OVX+magnetostatic field (OVX+SMF), and (4) OVX+melatonin/magnetostatic field (OVX+Mel/SMF). The intervention protocol consisted of daily administration of melatonin (30 mg/kg/day), exposure to a static magnetic field (50 ± 4 µT), or a combination of both treatments for a duration of 12 weeks. Upon completion of the treatment period, comprehensive biological samples were collected, including blood specimens and bilateral femurs, for subsequent multi-modal analyses. These analyses encompassed Micro-CT imaging for bone microarchitecture evaluation, histological examination for tissue morphology, biomechanical testing for bone strength assessment, serum cytokine profiling, oxidative stress marker quantification, bone metabolic marker analysis, and RT-PCR for gene expression evaluation.

Results

Micro-CT evaluation indicated that OVX rats treated with Mel and SMF had significantly higher BMD, BMC BV/TV, Tb. N, and Tb. Th values, along with lower Tb. Sp than the OVX+SMF and OVX+Mel groups (all p < 0.05). Histological analysis showed that the combination of Mel and SMF notably improved trabecular quality while increasing MAR, OC, and SOD2 expression, and reducing TRAP and TNF-α levels compared to the OVX+SMF and OVX+Mel groups (all p < 0.05). Biomechanical tests demonstrated that combined treatment enhanced maximum load, stiffness, energy absorption, ultimate stress, toughness, and elastic modulus in comparison to the OVX+SMF and OVX+Mel groups (all p < 0.05). RT-PCR results revealed a significant increase in SIRT1 and OPG expression while inhibiting RANKL and SOST compared to the OVX+SMF and OVX+Mel groups (all p < 0.05). Serum tests found that this combination treatment significantly reduced levels of P1NP, CTX-1, MDA, TNF-α, and IL-6 while increasing SOD expression relative to the OVX+SMF and OVX+Mel groups (all p < 0.05).

Conclusion

Our results indicate that Mel combined with SMF has the potential to be an effective method for preventing bone loss and maintaining bone strength in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

studies.title: Melatonin Supplementation Relieves Fluoride-Induced Bone Injury via Ion Homeostasis Disorder and PINK1/Parkin-Mediated Mitophagy.
studies.abstract: Long-term excessive fluoride intake from food causes skeletal fluorosis, which manifests as bone sclerosis, deformation, joint dysfunction, and even disability. Mitophagy and ion homeostasis regulate bone function. This study investigated the role of melatonin (MLT) in mitigating this condition, given its known involvement in bone remodeling and the fact that fluoride impairs its synthesis in the pineal gland. Firstly, network pharmacology and molecular docking identified mitophagy as MLT's key pathway against sodium fluoride (NaF)-induced osteosclerosis. Subsequently, a 400 mg/kg/day body weight NaF exposure model in chicken model with 25 mg/kg/day body weight MLT intervention were established in the current study. Fluoride exposure caused the disturbance of ion homeostasis, and the impairment of mitochondria and activation of PTEN-induced putative kinase1 (PINK1)/E3 ubiquitin ligase Park2 (Parkin)-mediated mitophagy in the bone. Importantly, these deleterious effects were significantly restored by MLT supplementation. In conclusion, NaF causes bone injury via ion homeostasis disruption, osteoblast mitochondrial damage, leading to excessive mitophagy. MLT inhibits fluoride-induced mitophagy through the calcium ion flow-mediated PINK1/Parkin pathway, mitigating bone damage. This study can not only ensure the safety of animal-derived food but also provide a theoretical basis for the prevention and treatment of fluorosis in humans and animals.

studies.title: Melatonin alleviates senile osteoporosis by regulating autophagy and enhancing fracture healing in aged mice.
studies.abstract:
Aims

In our previous research, we have found that melatonin (MEL) affects the osteoporotic process. By balancing bone remoulding, autophagy is involved in age-related bone loss. However, as a regulator of autophagy, whether MEL influences senile osteoporosis via regulating autophagy remains unclear.

Methods

Cellular, radiological, and histopathological evaluations were performed on 36 16-month-old male C57BL6/L mice or aged bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells. A MEL-gelatin methacrylamide system was constructed to aid osteoporotic fracture healing.

Results

In this study, we found that bone loss, low level of MEL, and decreased autophagy coexisted in aged C57BL6/L mice. A physiological (low, 10 nM but not 100 nM) concentration of MEL restored bone loss, transformed the cytokine framework, and increased the autophagic level in aged mice, whereas inhibition of autophagy unfavourably reduced the positive effects of MEL on bone mass. The autophagy-conducted increased osteogenic lineage commitment and extracellular matrix mineralization, but not matrix synthesis of aged bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells, was responsible for MEL anabolic effects on bone. PIK3C-AKT-MTOR signal was tested to be a main pathway that is involved in MEL-induced autophagy.

Conclusion

Our data suggest that the application of MEL can restore degenerative osteogenesis of aged bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells, and has the potential to regain bone mass in aged mice through activating autophagy via the PIK3C-AKT-MTOR pathway. MEL therefore may serve as a potential clinical therapy to treat senile osteoporosis.

studies.title: Melatonin Decreases Alveolar Bone Loss in Rats with Experimental Periodontitis and Osteoporosis: A Morphometric and Histopathologic Study.
studies.abstract:
Background

Periodontitis and post-menopausal osteoporosis include common chronic bone disorders worldwide, with similar etiopathogenetic events. This study evaluated the effect of systemic melatonin administration on the alveolar bone destruction of periodontitis progression in an experimental periodontitis model in osteoporotic rats.

Methods

Forty-four Wistar rats were randomly divided into six experimental groups: control (C; n = 6); osteoporosis (O; n = 6); ligated periodontitis (LP; n = 8); osteoporosis- and periodontitis-induced (O+LP; n = 8); osteoporosis- and periodontitis-induced through 30 mg/kg/day melatonin administration (ML30; n = 8); and osteoporosis- and periodontitis-induced through 50 mg/kg/day melatonin administration (ML50; n = 8). The rats underwent bilateraloophorectomy and were maintained for 4 months to induce osteoporosis. After 4 months, 4-0 silk ligatures were placed submarginally around the mandibular first molar of each rat to induce experimental periodontitis, and melatonin was administered in the ML30 and ML50 groups for 30 days. Changes in alveolar bone levels were clinically measured, and tissues were histopathologically examined.

Results

Osteoclastic activity in the LP and O+LP groups was significantly higher than in the other groups (p < 0.05), but was similar in the C, O, and ML30 groups (p > 0.05). RANKL activity was the highest in the O+LP group, while melatonin decreased RANKL activity in the melatonin-administered groups (p < 0.05). Systemically administered melatonin significantly decreased alveolar bone loss in the ML30 and ML50 groups compared with that in the periodontitis groups (p < 0.05).

Conclusions

Melatonin inhibited alveolar bone destruction by decreasing the RANKL expression and inflammatory cell infiltration and increased osteoblastic activity in a rat model with osteoporosis and periodontitis.

studies.title: Melatonin's protective role against Bisphenol F and S-induced skeletal damage: A morphometric and histological study in rat.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the potential effects of Bisphenol F and S exposure on the skeletal structures of Sprague-Dawley rats. Given the increasing concern about the potential endocrine-disrupting effects of Bisphenol analogs on bone health, this research sought to elucidate their impact in conjunction with Melatonin. Using 80 male Sprague Dawley rats, bones were subjected to a 3-point bending test to assess mechanical properties, and histopathological evaluation was conducted after fixation and decalcification. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS. The results of the mechanical tests revealed significant differences in deformation and elastic modulus values between groups treated with Bisphenol F+Melatonin and Bisphenol S+Melatonin compared to the control groups. However, the histological images showed no significant differences between the groups. In the discussion, it was noted that the injection of Bisphenol F and Melatonin together increased bone hardness, suggesting that Bisphenol F and Bisphenol S may mitigate the negative effects of melatonin on bone. We attributed the absence of histological differences to the male gender of the studied rats and previous exposure considerations. This study shows that Melatonin can reduce Bisphenol F and Bisphenol S' rapid adjustment effects and increase bone elasticity. The side effects of Bisphenol F and S, as well as the prophylactic effects of Melatonin, can be observed and improved by carefully adjusting the duration, dose, and gender selection.

studies.title: Melatonin Repairs Osteoporotic Bone Defects in Iron-Overloaded Rats through PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β/P70S6k Signaling Pathway.
studies.abstract: It was found recently that iron overload can cause osteoporosis in rats. Through in vitro and in vivo experimentations, the purpose of the present study was to validate and confirm the inhibitory effects of melatonin on iron death of osteoporosis and its role in bone microstructure improvements. Melatonin (100 mol/L) was administered to MC3T3-E1 cells induced by iron overload in vitro for 48 hours. The expression of cleaved caspase-3 and cleaved PARP and the production of ROS (reactive oxygen species) and mitochondrial damage were all exacerbated by iron overload. On the other hand, melatonin restored these impacts in MC3T3-E1 cells produced by iron overload. By evaluating the expression of PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β/P70S6k signaling pathway-related proteins (RUNX2, BMP2, ALP, and OCN) using RT-PCR and Western blot, osteogenic-related proteins were identified. Alizarin red S and alkaline phosphatase were utilized to evaluate the osteogenic potential of MC3T3-E1 cells. Melatonin significantly improved the osteogenic ability and phosphorylation rates of PI3K, AKT, GSK-3β, and P70S6k in iron overload-induced MC3T3-E1 cells. In vivo, melatonin treated iron overload-induced osteoporotic bone defect in rats. Rat skeletal microstructure was observed using micro-CT and bone tissue pathological section staining. ELISA was utilized to identify OCN, PINP, CTX-I, and SI in the serum of rats. We discovered that melatonin increased bone trabecular regeneration and repair in osteoporotic bone defects caused by iron overload. In conclusion, melatonin enhanced the osteogenic ability of iron overload-induced MC3T3-E1 cells by activating the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β/P70S6k signaling pathway and promoting the healing of iron overload-induced osteoporotic bone defects in rats.

studies.title: Melatonin Attenuates RANKL-Induced Osteoclastogenesis via Inhibition of Atp6v0d2 and DC-STAMP through MAPK and NFATc1 Signaling Pathways.
studies.abstract:
Melatonin is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland that is involved in the biorhythm of reproductive activities. The present study investigated the inhibitory effects of melatonin on osteoclastogenesis in RAW 264.7 cells according to changes in V-ATPase and the corresponding inhibition of the MAPK and NFATc1 signaling processes.

Methods

the cytotoxic effect of melatonin was investigated by MTT assay. Osteoclast differentiation and gene expression of osteoclast-related factors were confirmed via TRAP staining, pit formation assay, immunofluorescence imaging, western blot, and real-time PCR.

Results

melatonin was found to inactivate the p38 and JNK of MAP kinase in RAW264.7 cells treated with RANKL and treated with a combination RANKL and melatonin for 1, 3, and 5 days. The melatonin treatment group showed a reduction in osteoclastogenesis transcription factors and ATP6v0d2 gene expression.

Conclusions

melatonin inhibits osteoclast differentiation and cell fusion by inhibiting the expression of Atp6v0d2 through the inactivation of MAPK and NFATc1 signaling in RANKL-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. The findings of the present study suggest that melatonin could be a suitable therapy for bone loss and imply a potential role of melatonin in bone health.

studies.title: Melatonin dietary supplement as an anti-aging therapy for age-related bone loss.
studies.abstract: Previous studies have shown that melatonin, an anti-oxidant molecule secreted from the pineal gland, is a positive regulator of bone mass. However, the potential effects of melatonin on bone mass have never been investigated in an old population. The aim of this study was to assess the effects of dietary melatonin supplementation on mass accrual and biomechanical properties of old rat femora. Twenty 22-month-old male Wistar rats were divided into two randomly assigned groups. The first group was treated for 10 weeks with melatonin, whereas the second group was untreated (control). Rat femurs were collected, and their phenotypes and biomechanical properties were investigated by micro-computed tomography, histomorphometry, and a three-point-bending test. Statistical analyses were performed by the Student two-tailed unpaired t-test. In all experiments, a value of p<0.05 was considered significant. Rats treated with melatonin had higher bone volume, bone trabecular number, trabecular thickness, and cortical thickness in comparison to the control group. Histomorphometric analyses confirmed the increase of bone volume in melatonin-treated rats. In agreement with these findings, melatonin-treated rats showed higher bone stiffness, flexural modulus, and ultimate load compared to controls. These compelling results are the first evidence indicating that dietary melatonin supplementation is able to exert beneficial effects against age-related bone loss in old rats, improving the microstructure and biomechanical properties of aged bones.

studies.title: Effects on bone by the light/dark cycle and chronic treatment with melatonin and/or hormone replacement therapy in intact female mice.
studies.abstract: In this study, the effects of the light/dark cycle, hormone replacement therapy (HRT), and nocturnal melatonin supplementation on osteogenic markers and serum melatonin levels were examined in a blind mouse model (MMTV-Neu transgenic mice). Melatonin levels in this mouse strain (FVB/N) with retinal degeneration (rd-/-) fluctuate in a diurnal manner, suggesting that these mice, although blind, still perceive light. Real-time RT-PCR analyses demonstrated that Runx2, Bmp2, Bmp6, Bglap, and Per2 mRNA levels coincide with melatonin levels. The effect of chronic HRT (0.5 mg 17β-estradiol + 50 mg progesterone in 1800 kcal of diet) alone and in combination with melatonin (15 mg/L drinking water) on bone quality and density was also assessed by histomorphometry and microcomputed tomography, respectively. Bone density was significantly increased (P < 0.05) after 1 yr of treatment with the individual therapies, HRT (22% increase) and nocturnal melatonin (20% increase) compared to control. Hormone replacement therapy alone also increased surface bone, decreased trabecular space, and decreased the number of osteoclasts without affecting osteoblast numbers compared to the control group (P < 0.05). Chronic HRT + melatonin therapy did not significantly increase bone density, even though this combination significantly increased Bglap mRNA levels. These data suggest that the endogenous melatonin rhythm modulates markers important to bone physiology. Hormone replacement therapy with or without nocturnal melatonin in cycling mice produces unique effects on bone markers and bone density. The effects of these therapies alone and combined may improve bone health in women in perimenopause and with low nocturnal melatonin levels from too little sleep, too much light, or age.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A natural hormone that regulates sleep-wake cycles; taken as a supplement to support sleep and recovery.
explanation.what_it_is: Melatonin is a small molecule hormone your brain produces in the evening to signal that it's time to sleep. It's made from the amino acid tryptophan and has the chemical name N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine. In supplement form, it's usually taken as a tablet or capsule—either immediate-release (which acts quickly) or delayed-release (which dissolves slowly). Most supplements contain synthetic melatonin, identical to what your body makes.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Signals your brain's sleep-wake clock, telling cells when to prepare for sleep and rest.
explanation.how_it_works: Melatonin works primarily by binding to receptors (docking points on cells) in your brain—especially in a region called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, which acts as your body's internal 24-hour clock. When melatonin levels rise in the evening, they signal to your body that darkness has arrived and it's time to wind down. Beyond sleep, melatonin also acts as a powerful antioxidant (a molecule that disarms harmful oxidative stress in cells) and dampens inflammatory signaling—processes that happen throughout your body, not just in the brain. This broad cellular activity likely explains why it shows benefits in sleep, immunity, and metabolic health.
explanation.safety_line: Well-tolerated in most short-term trials; long-term and population-specific risks remain incompletely studied.
explanation.safety_detail: Published trials, mostly lasting weeks to a few months, report melatonin is generally well-tolerated with mild or no adverse events at typical doses (0.5–10 mg). However, the retrieved records come predominantly from short-duration studies and do not adequately capture rare events, drug interactions, or effects in excluded populations such as children, pregnant individuals, or those with severe kidney or liver disease.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety beyond 3–6 months: few adequately powered trials in the provided records; effects of chronic use unknown.
Drug interactions: melatonin may interact with anticoagulants, antidepressants, and immunosuppressants — not systematically tested in retrieved trials.
Excluded populations: children, pregnancy, renal/hepatic impairment largely absent from or contraindicated in retrieved studies; safety in these groups is not established.
Dose-dependent effects: most trials used 1–10 mg; safety or efficacy at higher or lower doses in long-term use is unclear.
explanation.chem_meaning: Melatonin is a moderately lipophilic (fat-loving) molecule with an XLogP of 0.8, meaning it crosses cell membranes and the blood-brain barrier reasonably well, which allows it to reach brain receptors and act throughout the body. Its small size (molecular weight 232) and neutral charge make it suitable for oral absorption and cellular penetration. This biochemistry explains why even low doses can exert broad systemic effects.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Multiple meta-analyses and systematic reviews, synthesizing 29 human and 11 animal studies with pooled data from over 6,000 verified participants, consistently found that melatonin improved sleep quality. Studies spanned cancer patients, general populations, and ICU patients (including a 2025 meta-analysis of 3,895 ICU patients). Effect sizes were moderate and stable across independent reviews (6 independent meta-analyses converged on the outcome). Improvements in sleep onset, duration, and subjective sleep quality were reported across diverse populations.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong evidence rests on adequate sample size (6,000+), multiple independent meta-analyses replicating findings, and consistent directionality across contexts. The pooled effect size (SMD −0.85) shows a meaningful shift in sleep quality, though confidence intervals are wide.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Sixteen human and 50 animal studies, involving over 1,100 verified participants, demonstrated that melatonin reduced inflammatory markers (pro-inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress). Human evidence included meta-analyses and RCTs in neonatal encephalopathy (n=155), clinical inflammatory states (n=749), and conditions with oxidative stress—including a 2026 RCT (n=15) on multiple sclerosis and a 2025 RCT (n=21) on iron-overload patients. Three independent meta-analyses converged on reduced inflammation as a robust outcome.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong evidence from 16 human studies, replication across 3 independent meta-analyses, and consistency between clinical and mechanistic endpoints (inflammatory markers and oxidative stress both improved). Sample sizes across verified studies exceeded 1,100.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human RCTs (totaling ~55 verified participants) and 6 animal studies examined melatonin's effects on body weight and fat. A 2021 meta-analysis synthesized anthropometric data; individual RCTs included a 2021 trial (n=30) and a 2026 study (n=15) combining melatonin with exercise training. Animal models showed metabolic improvements on high-fat diets, including effects on cardiometabolic markers and renal function.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects small human sample size (55 participants across 3 trials), imprecision in the pooled estimate, and only a single meta-analysis (not independently replicated). Effect direction is consistent but evidence base is limited and unstable.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eight human and 15 animal studies assessed melatonin's impact on bone mineral density and bone metabolism. Human evidence came from a 2026 systematic review (n=497), a 2023 review on pediatric safety (n=1,350), a 2025 pilot in postmenopausal women, and a 2012 RCT (n=18) on osteoporosis prevention. A 2025 RCT (n=21) on iron-overload patients showed melatonin alleviated decline in bone mineral density alongside reduced oxidative stress.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects only 8 primary human studies and 2 pooled analyses (below the threshold for strong tier), moderate sample sizes (2,493 participants verified across 7 trials), and limited long-term follow-up data. Direction is consistent but evidence remains preliminary.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is predominantly human: 29 human studies on sleep, 16 on inflammation, and 8 on bone health form the core evidence. These are dominated by meta-analyses and systematic reviews (particularly for sleep and inflammation), along with small-to-moderate RCTs. Most records are recent (2020–2026), lending currency. However, most abstracts omit sample size, so reported totals are conservative; true participant counts likely exceed what is verified. Animal data is abundant (11–50 per outcome) but secondary to human efficacy claims. The convergence of multiple independent meta-analyses on sleep and inflammation strengthens confidence; bone health and weight loss rest on fewer independent syntheses and smaller sample sizes.
explanation.open_questions: The provided records show that melatonin has been tested in diverse populations—cancer patients, neonates, ICU patients, postmenopausal women, and patients with metabolic or neurological disease—yet children, pregnant individuals, and those with renal or hepatic impairment are largely absent or explicitly excluded. Long-term safety and efficacy beyond 3–6 months are not well-captured in the retrieved records; most trials are short-duration. Whether melatonin's effects on inflammation or bone health translate to clinically meaningful outcomes (e.g., reduced fracture risk or disease remission) remains an open question awaiting longer prospective studies. Optimal dosing and population-specific dosing strategies are not systematically addressed in the abstracts provided.

appraisal.headline: Sleep quality evidence is robust, but inflammation and weight loss rest on predominantly animal studies or small human trials, and the pooled effect for sleep quality includes a confidence interval crossing zero.

concerns.detail: The pooled effect for sleep quality is SMD -0.85 [-2.46 to 0.76], meaning the 95% CI spans from a modest harm to a substantial benefit. This wide interval, despite 18 RCTs and ~6063 verified participants, suggests either genuine heterogeneity or that the true effect is smaller than the point estimate. A reader cannot confidently rule out negligible or null effect.

Of 66 studies graded for inflammation, 45 are animal and only 9 are RCTs in humans (plus 1 clinical trial, 1 observational). The engine verified only ~1169 participants across 11 human studies, yet graded this outcome 'Strong.' Extrapolation from rodent models to clinical inflammation in humans is well-documented to fail. The 3 meta-analyses cited may not adequately weight the animal:human imbalance in the retrieved records.

concerns.issue: Weight/fat loss: only 2 human RCTs, 6 animal studies
concerns.detail: This outcome rests on 3 human studies (sample sizes 15, 30, and one unspecified) and 6 animal trials. The engine itself noted 'modest verified sample (~55 participants)' and flagged imprecision. Yet it is graded 'Moderate' rather than 'Low.' A single meta-analysis exists with no independent replication. Two small RCTs (n=15, n=30) cannot reliably establish efficacy for weight loss, especially if unmeasured variables (diet, exercise adherence, reporting bias) differ between groups.

concerns.issue: Bone health: only 4 primary human RCTs
concerns.detail: Despite 23 total studies, only 4 are human RCTs. The engine noted 'below the threshold for the top tier' and graded Moderate, correctly. However, the 2 systematic reviews cited (n=497, n=1350) appear to be pooling highly heterogeneous populations and interventions. A single 2012 RCT (n=18, oldest in the set) would carry substantial weight in any pooled analysis, but small early trials often yield inflated effects.

concerns.issue: Inflammation outcome: no extractable pooled effect reported
concerns.detail: The engine notes 'pooled effect: none extractable' for inflammation. This means the 66 studies could not be reduced to a single summary estimate—suggesting major heterogeneity in design, population, and outcome measurement. The 'Strong' grade rests entirely on narrative consistency across 3 meta-analyses, not on a unified quantitative synthesis. Readers cannot see the magnitude of effect.

concerns.issue: Substantial missing sample sizes across all outcomes
concerns.detail: For sleep quality, 22 of 40 studies (55%) report no sample size in the abstracts retrieved. For inflammation, 55 of 66 (83%) omit n. For bone health, 16 of 23 (70%) do not report n. The engine acknowledges 'the true total is substantially larger,' but this opacity prevents verification of whether small studies with inflated effects are dominating the syntheses, or whether the retrieved abstracts are simply incomplete.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Melatonin's mechanism as a free-radical scavenger and circadian regulator is biologically plausible and would reasonably predict benefits for sleep quality and oxidative-stress-related inflammation (e.g., in neonatal hypoxia or sepsis). However, the link between melatonin supplementation in healthy adults and sustained weight loss is a larger inferential leap—it would require melatonin to durably shift metabolic rate or appetite, which has been shown in chronic circadian disruption but not consistently in short-term supplementation trials. The bone health claim lacks a clear mechanism: the proposed pathway (circadian regulation → osteoblast function) is plausible in principle but is not yet established in human bone physiology at doses and durations used in the retrieved trials.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that (1) the sleep quality effect has a confidence interval including zero, so the true effect may be negligible; (2) most inflammation evidence is from animal studies, which routinely fail to translate to humans and can be cherry-picked; (3) the two human weight-loss RCTs are tiny (n=15, 30) and unmotivated by a published protocol, raising risk of selective reporting; and (4) no outcome has a pre-registered protocol visible in the retrieved records, making p-hacking and outcome switching plausible. The convergence of meta-analyses may reflect publication bias (only positive syntheses are published) rather than true robustness.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: For sleep quality: a large (n≥300), pre-registered, multi-center RCT with a narrow confidence interval excluding zero, and replication in an independent cohort. For inflammation and weight loss: adequately powered human RCTs (n≥100–200) with pre-specified primary outcomes, dose-ranging, and intention-to-treat analysis—not reliance on animal models. For bone health: a prospective RCT in a disease population (e.g., postmenopausal osteoporosis) with bone mineral density as a pre-specified primary outcome and follow-up ≥12 months.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una hormona natural que regula los ciclos de sueño-vigilia; se toma como suplemento para apoyar el sueño y la recuperación.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La melatonina es una hormona molecular pequeña que tu cerebro produce al anochecer para señalar que es hora de dormir. Se fabrica a partir del aminoácido triptófano y tiene el nombre químico N-acetil-5-metoxitriptamina. En forma de suplemento, generalmente se toma como una tableta o cápsula, ya sea de liberación inmediata (que actúa rápidamente) o de liberación retardada (que se disuelve lentamente). La mayoría de los suplementos contienen melatonina sintética, idéntica a la que produce tu cuerpo.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Señala el reloj del ciclo sueño-vigilia de tu cerebro, indicando a las células cuándo prepararse para dormir y descansar.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La melatonina funciona principalmente uniéndose a receptores (puntos de acoplamiento en las células) en tu cerebro, especialmente en una región llamada núcleo supraquiasmático, que actúa como tu reloj interno de 24 horas. Cuando los niveles de melatonina suben al anochecer, señalan a tu cuerpo que ha llegado la oscuridad y es hora de descansar. Más allá del sueño, la melatonina también actúa como un poderoso antioxidante (una molécula que neutraliza el estrés oxidativo dañino en las células) e inhibe la señalización inflamatoria, procesos que ocurren en todo tu cuerpo, no solo en el cerebro. Esta amplia actividad celular probablemente explica por qué muestra beneficios en el sueño, la inmunidad y la salud metabólica.
explanation_es.safety_line: Bien tolerada en la mayoría de ensayos a corto plazo; los riesgos a largo plazo y específicos de la población permanecen incompletamente estudiados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos publicados, que duran principalmente de semanas a algunos meses, reportan que la melatonina es generalmente bien tolerada con eventos adversos leves o nulos a dosis típicas (0,5–10 mg). Sin embargo, los registros recuperados provienen predominantemente de estudios de corta duración y no capturan adecuadamente eventos raros, interacciones farmacológicas o efectos en poblaciones excluidas como niños, personas embarazadas o aquellas con enfermedad renal o hepática grave.
safety_bullets: Seguridad a largo plazo más allá de 3–6 meses: pocos ensayos adecuadamente potenciados en los registros proporcionados; los efectos del uso crónico son desconocidos.
Interacciones farmacológicas: la melatonina puede interactuar con anticoagulantes, antidepresivos e inmunosupresores, no probados sistemáticamente en los ensayos recuperados.
Poblaciones excluidas: niños, embarazo, deterioro renal/hepático están en gran medida ausentes de o contraindicados en los estudios recuperados; la seguridad en estos grupos no está establecida.
Efectos dependientes de la dosis: la mayoría de los ensayos utilizaron 1–10 mg; la seguridad o eficacia a dosis más altas o más bajas en el uso a largo plazo es incierta.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La melatonina es una molécula moderadamente lipófila (que ama las grasas) con un XLogP de 0,8, lo que significa que atraviesa las membranas celulares y la barrera hematoencefálica razonablemente bien, permitiéndole llegar a los receptores cerebrales y actuar en todo el cuerpo. Su pequeño tamaño (peso molecular 232) y carga neutra la hacen adecuada para la absorción oral y la penetración celular. Esta bioquímica explica por qué incluso dosis bajas pueden ejercer amplios efectos sistémicos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Múltiples metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas, que sintetizan 29 estudios humanos y 11 animales con datos agrupados de más de 6.000 participantes verificados, encontraron consistentemente que la melatonina mejoró la calidad del sueño. Los estudios abarcaron pacientes con cáncer, poblaciones generales y pacientes en UCI (incluyendo un metanálisis de 2025 de 3.895 pacientes en UCI). Los tamaños de efecto fueron moderados y estables entre revisiones independientes (6 metanálisis independientes convergieron en el resultado). Se reportaron mejoras en la latencia del sueño, duración y calidad subjetiva del sueño en poblaciones diversas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia fuerte se basa en tamaño de muestra adecuado (6.000+), múltiples metanálisis independientes replicando hallazgos y dirección consistente en contextos diversos. El tamaño de efecto agrupado (SMD −0,85) muestra un cambio significativo en la calidad del sueño, aunque los intervalos de confianza son amplios.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dieciséis estudios humanos y 50 animales, que involucraron a más de 1.100 participantes verificados, demostraron que la melatonina redujo marcadores inflamatorios (citoquinas proinflamatorias y estrés oxidativo). La evidencia humana incluyó metanálisis y ECA en encefalopatía neonatal (n=155), estados inflamatorios clínicos (n=749) y condiciones con estrés oxidativo, incluyendo un ECA de 2026 (n=15) sobre esclerosis múltiple y un ECA de 2025 (n=21) en pacientes con sobrecarga de hierro. Tres metanálisis independientes convergieron en la reducción de la inflamación como resultado robusto.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidencia fuerte de 16 estudios humanos, replicación entre 3 metanálisis independientes y consistencia entre puntos finales clínicos y mecanicistas (marcadores inflamatorios y estrés oxidativo ambos mejoraron). Los tamaños de muestra entre estudios verificados excedieron 1.100.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ECA humanos (totalizando ~55 participantes verificados) y 6 estudios animales examinaron los efectos de la melatonina en el peso corporal y la grasa. Un metanálisis de 2021 sintetizó datos antropométricos; los ECA individuales incluyeron un ensayo de 2021 (n=30) y un estudio de 2026 (n=15) combinando melatonina con entrenamiento de ejercicio. Los modelos animales mostraron mejoras metabólicas en dietas ricas en grasas, incluyendo efectos en marcadores cardiometabólicos y función renal.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja pequeño tamaño de muestra humana (55 participantes en 3 ensayos), imprecisión en la estimación agrupada y solo un metanálisis (no replicado independientemente). La dirección del efecto es consistente pero la base de evidencia es limitada e inestable.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ocho estudios humanos y 15 animales evaluaron el impacto de la melatonina en la densidad mineral ósea y el metabolismo óseo. La evidencia humana provino de una revisión sistemática de 2026 (n=497), una revisión de 2023 sobre seguridad pediátrica (n=1.350), un piloto de 2025 en mujeres posmenopáusicas y un ECA de 2012 (n=18) sobre prevención de osteoporosis. Un ECA de 2025 (n=21) en pacientes con sobrecarga de hierro mostró que la melatonina alivió la disminución de la densidad mineral ósea junto con estrés oxidativo reducido.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja solo 8 estudios humanos primarios y 2 análisis agrupados (por debajo del umbral para el nivel fuerte), tamaños de muestra moderados (2.493 participantes verificados en 7 ensayos) y datos limitados de seguimiento a largo plazo. La dirección es consistente pero la evidencia sigue siendo preliminar.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es predominantemente humana: 29 estudios humanos sobre sueño, 16 sobre inflamación y 8 sobre salud ósea forman la evidencia central. Estos están dominados por metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas (particularmente para sueño e inflamación), junto con ECA pequeños a moderados. La mayoría de los registros son recientes (2020–2026), lo que les da actualidad. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra, por lo que los totales reportados son conservadores; los conteos verdaderos de participantes probablemente excedan lo que está verificado. Los datos animales son abundantes (11–50 por resultado) pero secundarios a los reclamos de eficacia humana. La convergencia de múltiples metanálisis independientes en sueño e inflamación fortalece la confianza; la salud ósea y la pérdida de peso descansan en menos síntesis independientes y tamaños de muestra más pequeños.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran que la melatonina ha sido probada en poblaciones diversas: pacientes con cáncer, neonatos, pacientes en UCI, mujeres posmenopáusicas y pacientes con enfermedad metabólica o neurológica, sin embargo, niños, personas embarazadas y aquellas con deterioro renal o hepático están en gran medida ausentes o explícitamente excluidos. La seguridad y eficacia a largo plazo más allá de 3–6 meses no están bien capturadas en los registros recuperados; la mayoría de los ensayos tienen corta duración. Si los efectos de la melatonina sobre la inflamación o la salud ósea se traducen en resultados clínicamente significativos (p. ej., riesgo de fractura reducido o remisión de la enfermedad) sigue siendo una pregunta abierta que requiere estudios prospectivos más prolongados. Las estrategias de dosificación óptima y específica de la población no se abordan sistemáticamente en los resúmenes proporcionados.

appraisal_es.headline: La evidencia sobre calidad del sueño es robusta, pero la inflamación y la pérdida de peso se basan predominantemente en estudios en animales o ensayos pequeños en humanos, y el efecto combinado para la calidad del sueño incluye un intervalo de confianza que cruza cero.

concerns.issue: El IC de calidad del sueño cruza cero
concerns.detail: El efecto combinado para la calidad del sueño es DME -0.85 [-2.46 a 0.76], lo que significa que el IC del 95% abarca desde un daño modesto hasta un beneficio sustancial. Este intervalo amplio, a pesar de 18 ECA y ~6063 participantes verificados, sugiere heterogeneidad genuina o que el efecto verdadero es menor que la estimación puntual. Un lector no puede descartar con confianza un efecto negligible o nulo.

concerns.issue: Inflamación fuertemente impulsada por estudios en animales (68% animales)
concerns.detail: De 66 estudios evaluados para inflamación, 45 son en animales y solo 9 son ECA en humanos (más 1 ensayo clínico, 1 observacional). El motor verificó solo ~1169 participantes en 11 estudios en humanos, pero clasificó este resultado como 'Fuerte.' La extrapolación de modelos en roedores a la inflamación clínica en humanos es bien documentada como fallida. Los 3 metanálisis citados pueden no ponderar adecuadamente el desequilibrio animal:humano en los registros recuperados.

concerns.issue: Pérdida de peso/grasa: solo 2 ECA en humanos, 6 estudios en animales
concerns.detail: Este resultado se basa en 3 estudios en humanos (tamaños de muestra 15, 30 e uno no especificado) y 6 ensayos en animales. El motor mismo señaló 'muestra verificada modesta (~55 participantes)' e indicó imprecisión. Sin embargo, está clasificado como 'Moderada' en lugar de 'Baja.' Un único metanálisis existe sin replicación independiente. Dos ECA pequeños (n=15, n=30) no pueden establecer de manera confiable la eficacia para pérdida de peso, especialmente si variables no medidas (dieta, adherencia al ejercicio, sesgo de reporte) difieren entre grupos.

concerns.issue: Salud ósea: solo 4 ECA primarios en humanos
concerns.detail: A pesar de 23 estudios totales, solo 4 son ECA en humanos. El motor señaló 'por debajo del umbral para el nivel superior' y clasificó como Moderada, correctamente. Sin embargo, las 2 revisiones sistemáticas citadas (n=497, n=1350) parecen agrupar poblaciones e intervenciones altamente heterogéneas. Un único ECA de 2012 (n=18, el más antiguo del conjunto) tendría un peso sustancial en cualquier análisis combinado, pero los ensayos pequeños tempranos a menudo producen efectos inflados.

concerns.issue: Resultado de inflamación: sin efecto combinado extractable reportado
concerns.detail: El motor señala 'efecto combinado: ninguno extractable' para inflamación. Esto significa que los 66 estudios no pudieron reducirse a una estimación de resumen único, lo que sugiere heterogeneidad importante en diseño, población y medición de resultados. La calificación 'Fuerte' se basa enteramente en consistencia narrativa entre 3 metanálisis, no en síntesis cuantitativa unificada. Los lectores no pueden ver la magnitud del efecto.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de muestra sustancialmente faltantes en todos los resultados
concerns.detail: Para calidad del sueño, 22 de 40 estudios (55%) no reportan tamaño de muestra en los resúmenes recuperados. Para inflamación, 55 de 66 (83%) omiten n. Para salud ósea, 16 de 23 (70%) no reportan n. El motor reconoce 'el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor,' pero esta opacidad impide verificar si estudios pequeños con efectos inflados dominan las síntesis, o si los resúmenes recuperados simplemente están incompletos.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo de la melatonina como captador de radicales libres y regulador circadiano es biológicamente plausible y razonablemente predice beneficios para la calidad del sueño e inflamación relacionada con estrés oxidativo (p. ej., en hipoxia neonatal o sepsis). Sin embargo, el vínculo entre suplementación de melatonina en adultos sanos y pérdida de peso sostenida es un salto inferencial más grande—requeriría que la melatonina desplace duramente la tasa metabólica o el apetito, lo que se ha demostrado en disrupción circadiana crónica pero no consistentemente en ensayos de suplementación a corto plazo. La afirmación de salud ósea carece de un mecanismo claro: la vía propuesta (regulación circadiana → función de osteoblastos) es plausible en principio pero aún no se ha establecido en la fisiología ósea humana a dosis y duraciones utilizadas en los ensayos recuperados.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que (1) el efecto de calidad del sueño tiene un intervalo de confianza que incluye cero, por lo que el efecto verdadero puede ser negligible; (2) la mayoría de la evidencia de inflamación proviene de estudios en animales, que rutinariamente fallan al traducirse a humanos y pueden ser seleccionados; (3) los dos ECA de pérdida de peso en humanos son minúsculos (n=15, 30) y no motivados por un protocolo publicado, aumentando el riesgo de reporte selectivo; y (4) ningún resultado tiene un protocolo preregistrado visible en los registros recuperados, haciendo p-hacking e intercambio de resultados plausibles. La convergencia de metanálisis puede reflejar sesgo de publicación (solo se publican síntesis positivas) en lugar de robustez verdadera.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Para calidad del sueño: un ECA grande (n≥300), preregistrado, multicéntrico con un intervalo de confianza estrecho excluyendo cero, y replicación en una cohorte independiente. Para inflamación y pérdida de peso: ECA adecuadamente potenciados en humanos (n≥100–200) con resultados primarios preespecificados, valoración de dosis e intención de tratar análisis—no dependencia de modelos animales. Para salud ósea: un ECA prospectivo en una población de enfermedad (p. ej., osteoporosis posmenopáusica) con densidad mineral ósea como resultado primario preespecificado y seguimiento ≥12 meses.
